title: The ALMA REBELS survey: the dust-obscured cosmic star formation rate density at redshift 7
question: What is the typical fraction of dust-obscured star formation in UV-selected galaxies at z~7 and what is the dust-obscured cosmic star formation rate density at z~7?

data.sensitivity: line sensitivity L_[CII] ~ 2e8 L_odot at z=7 (5 sigma); continuum sensitivity sigma = 10 - 25 uJy beam^-1

what.value: Non-parametric stellar masses for the REBELS sample

evidence.quote: Given the greater flexibility offered by the non-parametric modelling, we adopt the (cite: topping2022) stellar masses for the REBELS galaxies throughout this work.

what.value: Dust continuum properties, detections, and positions of REBELS sources

evidence.quote: For further details on the dust continuum properties of the REBELS sources, we refer to (cite: inami2022).

evidence.loc: The Obscured Cosmic Star Formation Rate Density
evidence.quote: The procedure is as follows: we adopt the recent determination of the galaxy stellar mass function (SMF; denoted as $\Phi(M_\star)$) at $z=7$ from (cite: stefanon2021), thereby including the uncertainties on their derived SMF parameterization.

what.value: UV luminosities and UV star formation rates of REBELS targets

evidence.quote: Our sample is – by construction – rest-frame UV-detected, with its UV luminosities having been determined by Stefanon et al. (2022, in prep.), who additionally adopt the conversion factor to UV star formation rate of $\mathrm{SFR}_\mathrm{UV} / (M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1})= 7.1\times10^{-29} \times \left(L_\mathrm{UV} / (\mathrm{erg/s/Hz})\right)$.

what.value: Conversion from 158 um specific luminosity to total infrared luminosity

evidence.quote: In order to convert the flux densities to infrared luminosities, we adopt the conversion from (cite: sommovigo2022) derived specifically for REBELS.

To quantify this, we compare to the most recent dust-uncorrected UV-based SFRD measurements at $z\sim7$ from (cite: bouwens2022), who determine UV luminosity functions down to $M_\mathrm{UV} = -13$ aided by the gravitationally lensed galaxies observed across the Hubble Frontier Fields.

recipe.goal: Subtract bright serendipitous sources from continuum maps
recipe.method: Subtract two bright serendipitous galaxies ~5'' from the image centers of REBELS-05 and REBELS-P4 prior to stacking

recipe.goal: Sample stellar mass posteriors, flag starbursts, and bin sample
recipe.method: Approximate M_star posteriors as two-sided Gaussians, draw N_MC = 100 Monte Carlo realizations per galaxy, flag and exclude starbursts (>3x above extrapolated z=7 Schreiber et al. 2015 main sequence), and divide remaining galaxies into 4 stellar mass bins of 8-10 galaxies each (plus a no-MC fixed-median run)
key_parameters: 4 stellar mass bins with 8-10 galaxies per bin (or 2 bins each when splitting detections and non-detections)
Starburst threshold: SFR_UV+IR > 3 x main sequence at z=7 (excluding 8.5 +/- 2.1 out of 45 galaxies on average)

recipe.goal: Perform image-plane continuum stacking and measure stacked flux densities
recipe.method: Mean stacking in the image plane at native resolution centered on observed UV positions for continuum non-detections and rest-frame 158 um positions for detections; extract peak flux densities using source-finding software (cite: mohanrafferty2015) or compute upper limits
key_parameters: Peak threshold = 3 sigma, island threshold = 2 sigma
Upper limit = max{3 sigma, 3 sigma + S_pxl}
assumptions: Sources are unresolved by the ~1.3'' beam, so peak flux density equals total flux density

recipe.goal: Convert stacked flux densities to infrared luminosities, IR SFRs, and obscured fractions
recipe.method: Apply CMB correction at median stack redshift, convert rest-frame 158 um luminosity to L_IR and SFR_IR, compute f_obs = SFR_IR / (SFR_IR + SFR_UV), and fit linear f_obs - M_star relation
assumptions: L_IR = 11.7 (+4.1 / -2.3) * nu_0 * L_nu_0 (corresponding to modified blackbody with <T_dust> = 45 +/- 4 K and beta = 2.0)
SFR_IR / (M_odot yr^-1) = 1.2e-10 * (L_IR / L_odot) assuming constant SFR for 100 Myr, Z = 0.002, and Chabrier (2003) IMF
LambdaCDM cosmology with H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_m = 0.30, Omega_Lambda = 0.70, and Chabrier (2003) IMF

recipe.goal: Fit L_IR - M_star relation and integrate over z=7 SMF to derive obscured cosmic SFRD
recipe.method: Fit linear relation to log(L_IR) vs log(M_star) for each of the N_MC stacks using MCMC, then integrate Phi(M_star) * L_IR(M_star) over stellar mass and convert rho_IR to SFRD
key_parameters: Lower limit integration range: 8.8 <= log10(M_star / M_odot) <= 10.8
Full SFRD integration range: log10(M_star^lower / M_odot) = 8.2 (+0.7 / -2.1) (where f_obs = 0, floored at 5.0) to log10(M_star^upper / M_odot) = 12.4
assumptions: Stefanon et al. (2021) z=7 SMF shifted by -0.23 dex in stellar mass to convert from Salpeter (1955) to Chabrier (2003) IMF

answer_key.quantity: Obscured fraction at low stellar mass (log10(M_star/M_odot) approx 9.4)

evidence.loc: Obscuration across the full REBELS sample
evidence.quote: The obscured fraction determined for the REBELS sample ranges from $f_\mathrm{obs} = 0.33_{-0.04}^{+0.06}$ at low stellar masses ($\log_{10}\left(M_\star / M_\odot\right) \approx 9.4$) to $f_\mathrm{obs} = 0.58_{-0.18}^{+0.04}$ in the highest mass bin ($\log_{10}\left(M_\star / M_\odot\right) \approx 10.4$).

evidence.loc: Obscuration across the full REBELS sample

evidence.loc: Obscuration across the full REBELS sample
evidence.quote: Upon performing a linear fit to all $N_\mathrm{MC}$ samples and combining the posteriors, we determine a median slope and $16-84^\mathrm{th}$ percentile confidence interval of $0.27_{-0.15}^{+0.16}$ for the $f_\mathrm{obs} - M_\star$ relation.

answer_key.quantity: Typical obscured fraction of continuum-undetected REBELS sources

evidence.quote: In contrast to the dust detections, however, the continuum-undetected sources show significantly lower obscuration amounting to a typical $f_\mathrm{obs} \approx 0.25$.

Through a stacking analysis, we determine the typical obscured fraction of the continuum undetected sources to be $f_\mathrm{obs} \approx 0.25$ at a median stellar mass of $\log_{10}\left(M_\star/M_\odot\right) \approx 9.8$.

answer_key.quantity: Typical obscured fraction of continuum-detected REBELS sources

evidence.quote: In contrast, the detections exhibit a typical $f_\mathrm{obs} \approx 0.70$ at $\log_{10}\left(M_\star/M_\odot\right) \approx 10.0$.

score_reason: The high-level statistical, stacking, and MCMC integration methodology is thoroughly explained and tested against systematic variations, and all 6 ALMA project codes are listed. However, raw calibration and imaging details are deferred to companion papers, software names are obscured by LaTeX macro omissions in the text, and per-source input catalogs/maps are not tabulated directly in this article.
rediscovery_reason: All six ALMA project codes are public in the ALMA archive, the companion catalog papers (Bouwens et al. 2022, Inami et al. 2022, Topping et al. 2022) are published, and the main results (f_obs in mass bins, L_IR - M_star slope, and obscured SFRD at z~7) are clear numeric targets with a well-specified statistical recipe.
